precepts.text: And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself: and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined. Shall Messiah, that is Christ, be cut off, but not for himself. He did not die for himself. And the people of the prince that shall come: Rome.
precepts.point: He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken. Now, we might think that Christ does not understand what we are going through. I am going to show you that Christ knows perfectly well what we are going through. The whole chapter is talking about Christ, but I want to focus on verse 8. He was taken from prison and from judgment. He was cut off out of the land of the living: that is when he was crucified.
precepts.why:
“for he was cut off out of the land of the living”: that is when he was crucified. Daniel prophesied it: “And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself.” Messiah, that's Christ, is cut off, but not for himself. He didn't die for himself; Isaiah says, “for the transgression of my people was he stricken.”

“and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The people of the prince that shall come is Rome.

So the same Rome that dominated Israel when Christ was cut off came and destroyed the city and the sanctuary. Christ was cut off for the transgression of his people, and desolations were determined upon the city by the hand of Rome.

precepts.text: The open face: Daniel set his face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes. He understood by books, by the writings of Jeremiah the prophet, the number of the years. He went to the book, then made his confession: we have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, by departing from thy precepts. Neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets: they would not listen to the servants God sent to show them what they were doing wrong.
precepts.point: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory. When we behold the glass openly, we change. There is supposed to be a change in us.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
“But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord”. This book is the glass of the glory of the Lord, and we behold it with an open face. What is the open face? Daniel shows it: “And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes”. He went to God openly by prayer and supplication.

But first, “I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” Seeking God openly, he went to the book, the writings of Jeremiah. Then he made his confession: “We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments”.

“Neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets, which spake in thy name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.” They would not listen to the servants God sent to show them what they were doing wrong.

So when we really behold his face openly, we “are changed into the same image from glory to glory”. There is supposed to be a change in us when we pray, accept and understand that we have sinned against God. We behold ourselves in these books, and what we see there is there for us to fix. The worst thing to do is deny it, or refuse to hearken to the prophets he sends to show us how to get right.

precepts.text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to make reconciliation for iniquity. Reconciliation means to do again: it cannot apply to the other nations, because they were never a people close or near to God. The Israelites are the only ones that have been close or near to God, and through Christ we get our reconciliation. And if the slave masters wrote that God was the reconciled father of their slaves, that means they knew who we are.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The slave masters' directions said that God is their reconciled tender father. God is our reconciled father, but that reconciliation is not for everybody. What does re mean? To do again: repeat, redo. Reconcile means to do it again. So if they wrote that reconciliation was for the slaves, that means they knew who we are.

Reconciliation cannot apply to the other nations, because they were never a people close or near to God. The Israelites are the only ones that have been close or near to God. Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

That is determined upon Daniel's people and holy city, and the most Holy anointed is Christ. Through Christ we get our reconciliation. So the very masters who twisted Colossians 3:22 wrote down, in their own directions, that their slaves were the people God reconciles: Israel.

precepts.text: Seventy weeks, 490 years, are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins: meaning a major sacrifice would happen. To make reconciliation for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy: the Son of God.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.
precepts.why:
“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”: 490 years determined upon the Israelites and upon Jerusalem, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins.” To make an end of sins means a major sacrifice would happen.

“and to make reconciliation for iniquity”: to bring back the twelve tribes. “and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy”: to anoint the Son of God.

They said, well, we're not dealing with that; we're dealing with lambs, goats and bulls. Everybody see the problem? Daniel foretold one sacrifice that would make an end of sins, and that is the forgiveness of “all trespasses” in Colossians 2:13.

precepts.text: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. That is the anointing of the most Holy: Christ.
precepts.point: So Christ's seventy times seven is the 490: the prophecy completed, the perfection of mercy delivered exactly on schedule, because we could not sacrifice in our captivities and needed him.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ told Peter to forgive seventy times seven, and Christ never put numbers out just to put them there. Seven represents completion, but what is seventy times seven? Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. That is 490 years, from Persia to Christ, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

Who is the most Holy that is anointed? Hebrews 1:9 explains it: “Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” That is talking about Christ. Where Daniel says “to anoint the most Holy”, that is Christ.

So the seventy weeks run “unto the Messiah the Prince”, which is Jesus Christ, and the reconciliation for iniquity and the end of sins come through him. The prophecy was 490 years, completing that perfection through Christ, because we needed that mercy. We couldn't sacrifice when we were enslaved under Babylon and Persia; we were always in captivity, going from one captivity to the next, so we needed Christ.

The apostles said it: “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel”. That is why he told Peter to forgive his brother seventy times seven: because he forgave us seventy times seven. He is that complete perfection. But don't take him for granted.

precepts.text: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. The Roman armies: the desolation Daniel determined.
precepts.point: So Christ's seventy times seven is the 490: the prophecy completed, the perfection of mercy delivered exactly on schedule, because we could not sacrifice in our captivities and needed him.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: cut off for the children of Israel. “and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”. That prince that shall come and destroy the sanctuary is Titus. “and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The flood is 70 AD, the destruction, and us being led away into captivity.

Christ spoke of that same desolation: “And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” What armies? The Roman armies. That is what Daniel 9:26 is speaking of, the prince that shall come and destroy the city and the sanctuary.

Then Daniel 9:27: “in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”: the temple being destroyed. “and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation”. The Roman armies around Jerusalem were the sign that the desolation determined in the seventy weeks was at hand.

So the 490 years end with Christ cut off for us and the desolation of the city by Titus. After that there was no sacrifice for us but Christ, and that is why his sacrifice is our only way through to perfection.

precepts.text: After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.
precepts.point: He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week cause the sacrifice and oblation to cease, with the overspreading of abominations in the temple that Christ warned of. All seventy weeks are fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians the last week is future and belongs to a rebuilt temple, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures.
precepts.why:
Edom twists Daniel 9, so here is the code to break it down. Write it down: each day represents one year, each week represents seven years, and seventy weeks is 490 years. How do we know? Start with why Israel spent forty years in the wilderness.

“After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years”. The spies searched the land forty days. Because Israel sinned, they bore their iniquity forty years in the wilderness, a year for every day. “and ye shall know my breach of promise”: the Lord told them not to go up there, and they went up anyway.

That is the Lord himself counting a day for a year. So when Daniel is told “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”, those weeks are counted the same way: seventy weeks of seven days, every day a year, 490 years.

precepts.text: Thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days; I have appointed thee each day for a year.
precepts.point: He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week cause the sacrifice and oblation to cease, with the overspreading of abominations in the temple that Christ warned of. All seventy weeks are fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians the last week is future and belongs to a rebuilt temple, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures.
precepts.why:
The Lord gives the same count a second time, to Ezekiel: “thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days: I have appointed thee each day for a year.” Each day for a year. With Numbers 14 that is two witnesses to the code: a day in prophecy is a year.

Now Daniel 9 opens up. “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people”: seventy weeks equals 490 years. “from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks”: seven weeks plus sixty-two weeks is sixty-nine weeks, 483 years. That commandment started with Cyrus, when God told the Persians to let his people go to rebuild; Israel was hindered two years, then came Darius and Artaxerxes, and the building went on under Zerubbabel, Joshua, Ezra and Nehemiah, with Haggai and Zechariah. “the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times”: our forefathers caught hell from the nations and built with a sword in one hand and a brick in the other.

“after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: Christ crucified, not dying for himself but for the twelve tribes of Israel. “the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: Rome, in 70 AD. Then the last week: “he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”, and “for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate”, the abomination in the temple Christ warned about.

The total of seventy weeks has been fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians that last week has not happened yet and belongs to a rebuilt temple today, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures and going along with whatever they say because they are white. Counted a day for a year, the way the Lord counts it, all seventy weeks are done.

precepts.text: How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power. Christ is the most Holy anointed at the end of Daniel 9:24.
precepts.point: He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week cause the sacrifice and oblation to cease, with the overspreading of abominations in the temple that Christ warned of. All seventy weeks are fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians the last week is future and belongs to a rebuilt temple, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures.
precepts.why:
Seventy weeks are determined “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.” To make an end of sins is Christ coming to die, and the reconciliation for iniquity is all through Christ.

And who is the most Holy that is anointed? “How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.” Christ is the anointed one.

So the bottom of Daniel 9:24, “to anoint the most Holy”, is Christ, anointed as the most Holy. That is why the seventy weeks run unto “the Messiah the Prince”: the whole prophecy is counted to him and fulfilled in him.

precepts.text: O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, to the men of Judah and all Israel near and far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them because of their trespass.
precepts.point: The hypocrites of our people: Isaiah 9:16-17, the leaders of this people cause them to err, the religious and political leaders, T.D. Jakes and Pastor P, and they that are led of them are destroyed; the Lord has no joy in their young men nor mercy on their fatherless and widows, for every one is an hypocrite and evil doer and every mouth speaketh folly. They all have the Bible and say they believe in Jesus and do not one word of it.
precepts.why:
“Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.” Who are the far off? Daniel shows it's us.

“O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day.” The literal example: we were the top nation. Nations paid tribute to us under Solomon; David conquered everybody. Then we went into captivity, confused, and it was our sins that allowed it.

Bring it up to today. Our people go to school, get educated, get many degrees, and still are not accepted in this society. Now they are firing Black people with all those degrees: you're fired, we don't need you, DEI hire. And we say, but wait a minute, we did everything you told us to do. When we got away from them and built places like Black Wall Street and Seneca Village, they bombed us. They told us to fit in and get a good education; we did, and they still mock and scorn us. I assimilated, master, I'm one of you. That is confusion of faces.

“To the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them.” Look at our people: Dominicans and Cubans saying I voted for Donald Trump, and now it is backfiring on them. They haven't been touched yet, but they are going to be touched.

“Because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.” That is why we are the far off, driven through all the countries, and why Isaiah calls on us to hear what the Lord has done and acknowledge his might.

precepts.text: He shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation. Antiochus stopped Israel from serving God and destroyed the people. The Greeks, and the white man after them, are the abomination that maketh desolate.
precepts.point: In those times there shall many stand up against the king of the south; also the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision, but they shall fall. The robbers of thy people are the Caucasians, the Greeks then, who wanted the land of Israel and, as 1 Maccabees 3 shows, painted their likeness in the book of the law to rob our culture too. Judas Maccabeus rose against them. Today the ones in the land calling themselves Jews are the robbers, and they will fall the same way.

note.label: The Real Reason Iran Was Attacked

precepts.why:
“the robbers of thy people shall exalt themselves to establish the vision”. Who are the robbers of God's people? Daniel 9:27 shows what they do: “And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”. This is what Antiochus did: he stopped us from sacrificing and serving God.

“and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate”: he set up abomination and made our people desolate, meaning he destroyed our people, “even until the consummation”. That is why the Greeks, and the white man after them, are called the abomination of desolation, the abomination that maketh desolate. They are the robbers of God's people.

The Greeks wanted to conquer and take the land of Israel, and not only the land. First Maccabees 3 shows they took the book of the law and painted their likeness and their images in it, robbing us of our culture too. Judas Maccabeus rose up and fought against them.

And it is not only the Greeks. Christ said, “When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place”. In the time of the Greeks the abomination was the Greeks; in the time of Christ it was the Romans; and Europe is an extension of Rome. In 1949 Europeans from Germany, Poland, Russia and Ukraine went into the holy land saying, we are the people of God. Today the abomination of desolation is those people in the land calling themselves Jews and they are not: the Europeans, the Edomites. Why are they called that? Because they destroy everything; ask the Palestinians.

When they stand in the holy place, “then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.” They are the ones who will instigate it. But Daniel 11:14 ends, “but they shall fall.” The same way they fell back then is the same way they are going to fall today.

precepts.text: Seventy weeks, 490 years, are determined upon thy people and thy holy city, to finish the transgression, to make an end of sins, to make reconciliation for iniquity, atonement and justification, to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to anoint the most Holy. From the commandment to rebuild Jerusalem under Persia unto the Messiah the Prince under Rome; after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself, for his people, and the people of the prince that shall come, Titus and Vespasian, shall destroy the city and the sanctuary, with the end thereof a flood, 70 AD, and desolations determined as Israel is scattered.
precepts.point: It was not written for his sake alone, but for us also, to whom it shall be imputed, if we believe on him that raised up Jesus our Lord from the dead, who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification. Israel was accustomed to sacrificing; Paul says fine, but acknowledge Christ first, because if you put your faith in the animal and the temple falls, you have condemned yourself by default with no animal, no priest, and no temple.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Christ was delivered for our offences. Daniel shows the same thing on the prophetic clock: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. Seventy weeks, 490 years, upon thy people: Daniel’s people, Israel.

For what? “To finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.” That is what Christ did when he died. Reconciliation goes back to the word atonement, and back to the word justification.

“From the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem”: the rebuilding under Persia. “Unto the Messiah the Prince”: Rome. “And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”. He would be killed, but not for himself. Who was he killed for? His people. That is what Isaiah said, and that is why Daniel says not for himself.

“And the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: Titus and Vespasian. “And the end thereof shall be with a flood”: war, 70 AD. “And unto the end of the war desolations are determined”: Israel removed out of the land and scattered among all nations into slavery. When the temple was destroyed there was no priest and no temple left to atone with, so the one who put his faith in the animal instead of Christ condemned himself by default. Faith in Christ had to come first.

precepts.text: Confusion of faces to the men of Judah, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off.
precepts.point: That is why there should be no Christian church: Christ died only for Israel. Everything they quote about Gentiles and the world has already been shown to be Israel.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Who are the far off and who are the near? Daniel names them in his prayer: “O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them”.

Unto all Israel, that are near and that are far off. Both the near and the far off are Israel, driven through all the countries because of their trespass.

So when Ephesians says “ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ”, the far off are not the nations; they are Israel. Christ “hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us”, abolishing the enmity, the hatred between the southern and northern kingdoms, “for to make in himself of twain one new man”. Twain means two; the one new man is Israel, all twelve reconciled. “For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.”

precepts.text: O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee. That are where? And that are far off. To Israel that is near and that is far off. And it says that now we are made nigh to Christ Jesus.
precepts.point: Who was far off? Who was once close and then got distant, pushed away, cut off?
precepts.why:
Ephesians 2:13 says “ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who was far off? Who was once close, and then got distant, pushed away, cut off? Daniel answers it in his prayer.

“O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.” That are where? That are far off. The far off are Israel, driven into all the countries because of their trespass against the Lord.

So the far off of Ephesians are not other nations. They are Israel, both near and far off. Israel said, we are cut off for our parts, we have no hope. But now they do have hope, through Christ: the ones who were far off are made nigh by his blood.

precepts.text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy. So seventy weeks are determined upon thy people, the Israelites, and upon thy holy city, Jerusalem. And to make reconciliation for iniquity. So Christ dying brought reconciliation to God's people. It is very easy, very simple, very plain.
precepts.point: So reconcile means to restore friendly relations. I have a question. When was God ever on friendly terms with the other nations?
precepts.why:
“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

Thy people are the Israelites, and thy holy city is Jerusalem. Within those seventy weeks the Lord would make an end of sins and “make reconciliation for iniquity.” That reconciliation was determined upon Daniel’s people, not upon the other nations.

So when Ephesians says Christ came to “reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby,” it is the fulfilling of Daniel. Christ dying brought reconciliation to God’s people, Israel. It is very easy, very simple, very plain.

precepts.text: All Israel had transgressed the law, so the curse and oath written in the law of Moses was poured out upon them, for the Most High is righteous in all his works.
precepts.point: He knows great is the wrath of the Lord poured out because the fathers had not kept the word of the Lord to do all that is written in the book. To inquire of the Lord, one must go to a saint, a chosen prophet who has the word.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“Yea, all Israel have transgressed thy law, even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him.” The Lord “hath confirmed his words, which he spake against us”, “for the Lord our God is righteous in all his works which he doeth: for we obeyed not his voice.”

Josiah saw the same thing when he heard the book: “it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the law, that he rent his clothes”, and said, “great is the wrath of the Lord that is poured out upon us, because our fathers have not kept the word of the Lord, to do after all that is written in this book.”

All Israel had transgressed the law, so the curse and oath written in the law of Moses was poured out upon them, and the Most High is righteous in it. Josiah knew it, so he sent to “enquire of the Lord for me, and for them that are left in Israel and in Judah”.

precepts.text: He confirmed his words against us and our judges by bringing on us a great evil, not against all people but against us, as was done upon Jerusalem, who are the Israelites.
precepts.point: He will save the afflicted people but bring down high looks. Israel is the afflicted people the scripture is talking about.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“For thou wilt save the afflicted people; but wilt bring down high looks.” Israel is the afflicted people the scripture is talking about, and Daniel shows why we are the afflicted: “And he hath confirmed his words, which he spake against us, and against our judges that judged us, by bringing upon us a great evil: for under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.”

He confirmed his words against us and against our judges by bringing on us a great evil. Not against all people, but against us, as was done upon Jerusalem, who are the Israelites. Nothing under the whole heaven has been done like what was done to us.

With the froward he shows himself froward, and we were froward. But he is the one who will save the afflicted people, and bring down the high looks of those over us.

precepts.text: Righteousness belongs to the Most High but confusion of faces to all Israel scattered in the countries because they trespassed.
precepts.point: They will call us any name we want except Esau, as long as we keep celebrating Christmas, Thanksgiving, New Year's, the 4th of July, and birthdays. If they keep us in sin, the Most High will not fight our battles.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“My confusion is continually before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me”. Daniel confesses the same thing for the whole nation: “O Lord, righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.” Righteousness belongs to the Most High, but confusion of faces to all Israel scattered through all the countries, because we trespassed.

When the enemy looks at us now, they no longer see a perfection of beauty. They see men sagging their pants, women dressed immodestly, whoredom in the songs, and they shake their heads. That is the confusion of faces, and it is because of our trespass.

precepts.text: Departing from the precepts and the judgments of the Most High is sin, as Israel confessed they had done wickedly and rebelled by departing from His precepts.
precepts.point: Once we depart from the precepts we are in the midst of sin. The prayer here is that our ways were directed to keep His statutes, so that we shall not be ashamed when we have respect unto all His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Thou hast commanded us to keep thy precepts diligently.” The word precept means law, commandment, rule. That is what a precept is, so precept upon precept is talking about the word of the Most High, the scriptures, the law.

Daniel shows what departing from them is: “We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments”. Israel confessed that they had done wickedly and rebelled, and the rebellion was departing from his precepts.

Once we depart from the precepts we are in the midst of sin. That is why the prayer is “O that my ways were directed to keep thy statutes!”: to keep them diligently and not be ashamed, having respect unto all his commandments. Blessed are the undefiled in the way, because without the law we are defiled.

precepts.text: The Most High shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.
precepts.point: Our people were scattered everywhere because of our transgressions, exactly as the law warned.
precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” That is the law's warning, and Daniel's prayer is the warning fulfilled. Confusion of faces belongs “to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.”

Our people were scattered everywhere because of our transgressions, exactly as the law warned. Daniel lays it where it belongs, on us: “to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against thee.” The scattering from one end of the earth to the other came because we rebelled: “Neither have we obeyed the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.”

And yet “To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against him”. Righteousness is his, confusion of face is ours, and mercy is still his to give.

precepts.text: If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Most High to do his commandments, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee.
precepts.point: The oath that was written is Deuteronomy 28, verses 1 through 68.
precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. This is the oath Daniel is confessing: “the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him.” The oath that was written is Deuteronomy 28, verses 1 through 68, and verse 15 is where the curses begin.

All Israel transgressed the law “even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice”. That is not hearkening to the voice of the Lord, and the curses came upon them and overtook them just as Moses wrote. The Lord “confirmed his words, which he spake against us” by bringing a great evil, “for under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.”

Even so, “yet made we not our prayer before the Lord our God, that we might turn from our iniquities, and understand thy truth.” The Most High is righteous in all his works: the curse was written in the law before the evil came, and it came because “we obeyed not his voice.”

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
Another one on reading. “In the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” Daniel said, I Daniel understood by books. What books was he reading? The previous books of the previous prophets. Daniel occupied himself studying, so he said, based upon the writings of Jeremiah we're going to be in Babylon 70 years. And it was so, and it was true, and not one word failed: it was 70 years to the day that that captivity was, and then Persia took over.

So when you got the book in your hand or in your house and you don't occupy yourself with reading, you're a fool. This is why: read at least four chapters a day. At least, minimum; that's a minimum, four chapters a day.

points: All Israel have transgressed thy law; therefore the curse is poured upon us, the curses of Deuteronomy 28:15-68, and the oath written in the law of Moses, because we have sinned against him. note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: The code: each day a year, each week seven years, seventy weeks 490 years. Numbers 14:34 gave forty years for forty days of searching the land, and Ezekiel 4:6 appointed each day for a year.

Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and thy holy city to finish the transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up the vision, and anoint the most Holy. That is Christ, whom God anointed with the Holy Ghost and power, Acts 10:38.

From the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem, which began under Cyrus and was hindered two years until Darius and Artaxerxes, with Zerubbabel, Joshua, Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai, and Zechariah, unto the Messiah the Prince is seven weeks and sixty-two weeks, 483 years. The street and wall were built in troublous times, a sword in one hand and a brick in the other.
After the sixty-two weeks Messiah is cut off, but not for himself: he died for the twelve tribes. The people of the prince that shall come, Rome, destroyed the city and the sanctuary in 70 AD.

He shall confirm the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week cause the sacrifice and oblation to cease, with the overspreading of abominations in the temple that Christ warned of. All seventy weeks are fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians the last week is future and belongs to a rebuilt temple, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures.
Unto us confusion of faces, as at this day, to the men of Judah and all Israel, near and far off. Bleached skin, dyed hair and surgery are the confusion Esau has put on the people.

points: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, made king over the realm of the Chaldeans, Daniel understood by the books the seventy years of the desolations of Jerusalem spoken to Jeremiah.
This is the same Darius dealt with when the Persians and Medes were shown in chapters 7 and 8.

Daniel set his face unto the Most High to seek him by prayer and supplications, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes, confessing that the people had sinned, committed iniquity, done wickedly, and rebelled, departing from his precepts and judgments.
They had not hearkened unto the prophets who spake in his name to their kings, princes, fathers, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to the Most High, but confusion of faces to the people of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, near and far off, driven through all the countries because of their trespasses.
To the Most High belong mercies and forgiveness, though the people had rebelled and had not obeyed his voice to walk in his laws set before them by the prophets.
All Israel transgressed the law by departing, so the curse was poured upon them and the oath written in the law of Moses, because they had sinned against him.
The oath that was written is Deuteronomy 28, verses 1 through 68.

He confirmed his words by bringing upon them a great evil, for under the whole heaven none was done as was done upon Jerusalem, yet even so they had not made their prayer to turn from their iniquities. The Most High is righteous in all his works.

Daniel appealed to the Most High who brought his people out of Egypt with a mighty hand, confessing they had sinned and done wickedly, and asking that his anger and fury be turned away from his city Jerusalem, his holy mountain.
He pleaded for the Most High to hear, forgive, hearken, and do, not for their righteousness but for his great mercies, since the city and the people are called by his name.

While Daniel was speaking, praying, and confessing his sin and the sin of his people Israel, the man Gabriel, whom he had seen in the vision, was caused to fly swiftly and touched him about the time of the evening oblation.
Gabriel came to give him skill and understanding, for at the beginning of his supplications the commandment came forth, and Daniel was greatly beloved.

Seventy weeks are determined upon the people and the holy city to finish the transgression, make an end of sins, make reconciliation for iniquity, bring in everlasting righteousness, seal up the vision, and anoint the most Holy.

Daniel was given the four beasts first, then this further vision of the seventy weeks by Gabriel in the midst of his prayer and supplications. The bishop's class on the seventy weeks opens this up in full.
From the going forth of the commandment to restore and build Jerusalem unto Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks and threescore and two weeks, the street built again even in troublous times.

After threescore and two weeks Messiah is cut off, but not for himself, and the people of the prince that shall come destroy the city and the sanctuary. He confirms the covenant with many for one week, and in the midst of the week causes the sacrifice and oblation to cease.
